head: fb79950
target: A scenario file drives a headless run whose result directory is the whole input to grading, and grading splits engine bugs from model mistakes.
incidental: the npm bin entry and the script that loads the .env file
the boundary test adjusted so it still guards the eval code's imports
the fixture plugins and the weather scenario file under the test scenarios directory
the three test files, whose case tables are keyed by the check names

questions.prompt: The live weather test was a hard-coded script. Why did it become a scenario file?

options.label: multeval passes a single instruction string, so the scripted session must travel as a file.
So the model can read the plan and follow the steps itself.
So a run needs no plugin code loaded from the disk.
Because the hard-coded live test could not call a real model.

key_points: multeval hands aigent a single instruction string, so a whole scripted session must live in a file.
A scenario holds prompt, host enable and resume steps over one session.
Each prompt's expected behaviors are written beside it in the file.

questions.prompt: After a run, the command grades the result directory it just wrote, never its memory. What does that prove?

options.label: Every run shows the files alone are enough to grade it, so an outer grader can trust them.
Reading the files back is faster than grading the run in memory.
The files hold more than the runner kept in memory.
A report read from files comes out the same for every model provider.

key_points: Every run proves the files alone are enough to grade the run, so the write path is tested each time.
The outer grader reads the same files and gets the same verdict as the runner.
A bug in the write shows up on the run that made it, not later on the grader.

questions.prompt: Why does the report judge engine invariants and model behaviors on different rules?

options.label: One broken invariant is an engine bug; a missed behavior is one point in a rate.
Invariants read the transcript, and behaviors read the session events.
Invariants are declared in a scenario file, and behaviors are built in.
Behaviors are judged only after every invariant has passed.

key_points: An invariant is an engine property every run must keep; one failure is an engine bug.
A behavior is a bet on the model, judged per prompt and measured as a rate over runs.
Cost is reported and never judged.
Behaviors never change the exit code; they are rates, not gates.

questions.prompt: A model answers one prompt without enabling the weather plugin, and the run stops before a later prompt. Which verdicts does the report mark as skipped? Pick all that apply.

options.label: The check that the model calls the weather tool
The check that the model enables the weather plugin
A behavior on the prompt that never ran
Every invariant on the run

key_points: A behavior skips when its precondition never happened, such as a call check without the enable it needs.
A behavior skips on any step the run never reached.
A skipped behavior is left out of its rate, which counts only trials that had the chance.
Invariants never skip; a run with nothing to check passes.

questions.prompt: The checks read the transcript and the session events together. What goes wrong if they read only one of them?
key_points: Only the transcript shows the records a session writes at creation; no listener can subscribe in time to see them.
Only the transcript shows a call the engine rejected before it ran; such a call leaves no tool event.
The events carry what listeners saw: the calls of each turn and each tool outcome with its denial.
Reading one record alone, the checks would misjudge some runs the other record explains.

questions.prompt: Why does the runner refuse some scenarios before the first session opens?

options.label: One pass names every problem at its place in the file, so a mistake costs no model call.
The engine cannot load a plugin directory after the first session opens.
A scenario with problems would make the result directory unreadable.
The model would refuse a prompt from a scenario that has unknown fields.

key_points: Unset secrets, a plugin set that will not load, and names the sets lack are refused before the run starts.
A mistake in a scenario must cost no model call, because model calls cost money.
Every problem is reported at its place in the file, in one pass, so an author fixes the file in one round.
Unknown fields are problems too, so a misspelled expectation cannot silently disappear.

questions.prompt: The session already hides secret values from listeners. Why does the runner scrub the run log again?

options.label: A leaked value still never reaches the files, and the mark names the leak without the key.
The session's redaction covers only tool results, so the events need a second pass.
The scrub hides which secrets a scenario uses, so the model cannot ask for them.
The transcript goes back to the model provider, so it must be cleaned twice.

key_points: The session's redaction is the engine's own promise, and the scrub is the net that catches the engine breaking it.
Even a leaking engine cannot put a raw secret value into the run log or the files.
The scrub leaves a mark that names the secret, so a grader without the key still sees the leak.

questions.prompt: A run stops early, and its report also shows one failed invariant. What exit code does the caller see, and why?

options.label: 1: an engine bug is the worse news, so it wins over stopped-early
3: the run stopping early is the first thing the caller must fix
4: the runner itself failed to finish its work
2: the scenario must have been bad, since the run went wrong

key_points: Exit 1 means an invariant failed, which is an engine bug.
An engine bug matters more than a run that stopped early, so its code wins.
The stopped run was still written and checked, so its report and files exist.

questions.prompt: The runner is killed while it writes the result directory. What does the next reader see?
key_points: The files go to a sibling directory first and are renamed into place only once they are complete.
So the reader sees either a whole run or no directory at all.
A crash can leave a sibling with partial in its name, which no reader mistakes for a run.

questions.prompt: A provider timeout stops a run after two of four prompts. What can the outer grader still learn from the result directory?
key_points: The steps that ran were written, and the grader can grade the run from the files alone.
The report says the run is not complete, and the exit code says stopped early, not engine bug.
Behaviors on the aborted prompt and the unreached ones skip, so their rates leave this run out.
The invariants are judged as usual, so an engine bug would still show.
